issues.evidence: A single quote-state scanner masks RFC-quoted payload before structural H2H signature detection, including across embedded physical newlines. Real shared clauses and (none) outside quotes still route to strict H2H parsing.

RFC-vs-whitespace dispatch ignores comma and quote punctuation on full physical comment lines whose first non-whitespace character is #. Comment masking is quote-state-aware, so a # line inside a multiline RFC field remains data.

The legacy unescaped H2H exporter now emits only its characterized lossless identifier subset. An unrepresentable hyperedge or shared-vertex identifier produces an explicit non-generated diagnostic instead of silently corrupt text.

hyperedgeIdentifiers.representableRule: A non-empty identifier with no leading/trailing whitespace, CR/LF, structural colon, or opening square bracket, and which does not begin with #.
hyperedgeIdentifiers.contextNote: A # prefix can appear to survive when another neighbor row reintroduces the ID, but an isolated source line is discarded as a comment; it is therefore not globally representable.

sharedVertexIdentifiers.representableRule: A non-empty token with no whitespace, comma, or closing square bracket. Numeric-looking tokens must import as a finite number whose canonical string is identical to the exported token.

h2hRepresentability.futureOwner: A future explicitly approved H2H format-design stage
h2hRepresentability.futureWork: Introduce a versioned escaping/quoting grammar only with old-format compatibility and complete import/export round-trip tests. No new syntax was invented in this corrective pass.
